proposals.label: Ship-blessing preparation room
proposals.imageDirection: A tidesage preparation room in a stone building near the valley’s shipbuilding coast. Long blue-green robes hang on wooden pegs above folded sailcloth; a broad table holds carved shell vessels, braided cords, brass bells, sea-polished stones and bowls of clean seawater. Pale spiral carvings and wave-shaped lintels repeat through thick coastal architecture. High windows admit cool silver light, with green hills and a mast visible beyond. A small lamp warms the textile corner. Compose a working sacristy for ritual preparation and garment care, detailed with oceanic craftsmanship, folded textiles and fine hand-finished ritual implements.
proposals.context: Robes hang above folded cloth where salt damp can dry from their hems. Bells, braided cords and shell vessels are arranged on the preparation table beside bowls of seawater. The door separates the room from louder activity outside; cloth, wood and water give it a clean, restrained scent.

proposals.label: Energy-cell charging bay
proposals.imageDirection: A crowded Mechagon charging room assembled from bolted plates, cylindrical sockets and mismatched insulated cabling. Rows of removable energy cells stand in brass-and-steel cradles below blue indicator lamps; big ceramic switches and a rolling counter mark the handover station. Weathered orange panels, oil stains and handwritten repair tags contrast with precise electrical components. A thick window shows grey island rock, conifers and scrap heaps beyond the wall. Copper pipes run overhead into a buzzing regulator. Keep the forms eccentric, ingenious and robust, with a small safe waiting alcove behind a waist-high guard rail.
proposals.context: Energy cells stand in charging cradles along the wall. Indicator lamps mark the sockets, and a low electrical hum runs through the regulator overhead. The room smells of warm metal and old oil; conversation is possible beside the desk, farther from the regulator’s persistent buzz.

proposals.label: Recycler sorting room
proposals.imageDirection: A Mechagon recycling interior centred on an absurdly substantial feed hopper and a squat machine with exposed springs, grinding teeth and a glowing status dial. Sorting tables hold machined gears, hardened springs and stacks of tempered plates in different trays. A chute delivers reclaimed metal to wheeled bins along riveted orange-grey walls. Hanging work lamps and a dirty skylight illuminate clipped cables, chipped paint and greasy handprints. Beyond a heavy open door appear conifers, rock and heaps of salvage. Place a protected inspection ledge beside the sorting counter, clear of the machinery’s emphatic moving parts.
proposals.context: Components are sorted into trays before reaching the recycler’s feed hopper. Springs, gears and plating make different piles on the tables, while reclaimed material gathers in wheeled bins below the discharge chute. The machine vibrates through the floor when it runs, and speech is easier from the inspection ledge than beside its grinding housing. Dust and old grease mark the working surfaces. A clear stretch of counter provides room to examine a piece before deciding where it belongs.
proposals.availability: Mechagon; functioning recycling premises using compatible technology, with a safe accessible sorting area. Require actual operational machinery for vibration and grinding audio; use an idle-text variant during shutdown. No named recycler or scripted malfunction.

proposals.label: Augmentation fitting room
proposals.imageDirection: A compact Mechagon augmentation clinic, ingenious and slightly over-equipped: a padded reclining chair beneath an articulated lamp, wall racks of polished mechanical hands and joints, and a rolling tray of delicate screwdrivers beside massive clamp arms. Brass measuring gauges, diagrams of limb interfaces and labelled oil bottles cover a riveted workbench. Teal indicator lights reflect from clean steel amid older orange-painted panels. A side chair and a curtained changing recess provide personal space. Through a porthole appear island pines and grey stone. proposals.context: The padded chair sits beneath a jointed inspection lamp. Small tools and measuring gauges occupy a clean tray, while replacement joints are kept in separate padded drawers. Oil has a sharper smell here than in the curtained changing recess. A visitor’s chair stands beside the workbench, close enough for quiet discussion of fit, movement and repairs. Screens offer some privacy from the entrance, and detachable parts can be laid out without sharing space with coats or travelling bags.
proposals.availability: Mechagon; an operating mechanical-augmentation maintenance clinic with relevant trained services and compatible bodily technology. Require an accessible consultation/fitting room. Do not assume anyone has augmentations, consents to a procedure or follows King Mechagon’s ideology.

proposals.label: Island fish-smoking kitchen

A preparation slab and low dining bench share the dry timber floor, while baskets and covered water jars stay away from the hearth. proposals.context: The kitchen smells of wood smoke and preserved fish. Woven wind screens soften the sea breeze without enclosing the room completely. Voices near the bench remain audible to the adjoining preparation space. Behind the stored baskets, a closer exchange can accompany the practical business of arranging meals, provisions or the use of a scarce cooking hearth.

proposals.label: Kodo harness-fitting hall
proposals.imageDirection: Create a broad, heavily roofed animal-handling hall at the edge of tawny savanna. Huge stall arches and stout rounded posts fit kodo bulk, while oversized padded harness hangs from wide beams above loading frames and woven fodder baskets. A fitting bay opens directly onto a spacious corral; a small weighing bench holds straps, buckles and ownership records. Flat-crowned trees and distant blue-gray ridges show beyond the doorway. Warm leather, dust and worn timber dominate; the building’s extraordinary animal scale distinguishes it from a conventional human stable.
proposals.context: Oversized harness hangs from heavy beams above broad fitting bays. Padded straps, loading frames and fodder baskets show the work needed to turn a great beast into reliable transport. The corral opens toward the tawny plain, while the weighing bench provides room to examine a harness or settle an animal’s hire and carrying terms. The hall leaves demonstrations visible from the entrance. Between the covered stalls, a quieter exchange can address condition, ownership, damage or responsibility for a valuable caravan beast.
proposals.availability: Barrens settlement with a maintained kodo husbandry or caravan stable, stocked harness and access to kodos. Existing stable form may persist after a culture change; no specific caravan event is required.

proposals.label: Oasis water-division shelter

Narrow channels, removable barriers and clearly marked measuring stones separate domestic draw-off from maintained watering troughs. A deep shade roof covers a counter with allocation tallies and simple gauges, while dry grassland and flat-crowned trees stretch beyond the concentrated green. Leave the basin usable and accessible, with maintenance tools stored against a low wall. The image should emphasize locally organized water distribution, not a luxurious fountain or general caravan yard.

proposals.label: Savanna cartel contracting office
proposals.imageDirection: Show a cramped goblin-built contracting room overlooking gold savanna through thick slatted shutters. A tiny oversized-in-importance desk bristles with contract rolls, fee notices, stamped receipts and a many-drawered cash cabinet. Riveted safes, brightly colored commercial plaques, a sample machine part and an ostentatiously gilded chair advertise ambitious frontier enterprise. A secure grille separates the signing counter from collateral storage. The low, cluttered room makes its grandiose display comic and acquisitive, while the dusty acacia landscape outside keeps it a Barrens establishment rather than a metropolitan bank.
proposals.context: Contract rolls, stamped receipts and notices of fees crowd the signing counter. A gilded chair stands behind a narrow desk, backed by locked drawers and a riveted safe. Through the shutters lies the tawny savanna; within, even a sample machine part occupies display space. The grille makes the distinction between negotiation and secured property unmistakable. Terms, collateral, repairs and responsibility can be argued over tangible documents. The counter keeps the exchange formal, while a cramped side desk permits discussing a more exclusive offer.
proposals.availability: Barrens settlement with an operating goblin/cartel-style contracting or finance office, literate commercial administration and mechanical metal fittings. Cartel affiliation comes from current institutions, not the region name.

proposals.label: Captain’s counting room
proposals.imageDirection: A private maritime counting room in a tropical pirate residence: a broad scarred table covered with balance scales, loose coin stacks, mixed trade goods and an opened cargo ledger. The room has enough space to lay out belongings for inspection, but the inner cabinet and heavy door keep the most secure storage separate.

Cups and personal belongings compete for table space, while the galley’s hot corner is best approached from the clear end of the counter.

proposals.label: Jungle fibre-weaving room
proposals.imageDirection: A breezy fibre-working room in a tropical island dwelling, its deep roof carried by thick dark posts above raised plank flooring. Long strips of leaf fibre hang from the rafters beside baskets of dyed cord, half-finished carrying straps and a broad wooden weaving frame. Moss-green stone footings show beneath the doorway, with bright broadleaf jungle and vine-wrapped trees immediately outside. Clay dye bowls add ochre, rust and dark blue to the natural green-brown palette. A low bench and a clear working mat provide intimate seating. Dye bowls occupy their own low shelf, and visitors can leave wet baggage at the threshold before joining the work.

proposals.label: Rainwater cistern chamber
proposals.imageDirection: A cool cistern chamber beneath a small tropical island house, built from broad moss-stained green-grey blocks with heavy timber roof supports. Rainwater enters through a stone-lined channel and settles in a covered central basin. Clay jars, wooden buckets, a sand-filter tray and a raised dry shelf occupy the sides. A shaft of daylight from the entrance catches fern shadows and tiny droplets on the masonry. Roots press against the exterior steps, linking the room to the thick jungle above. Keep the architecture low, robust and practical, with the basin’s still surface providing the central visual focus.
proposals.context: Rainwater reaches the covered basin through a narrow channel. Buckets and closed jars stand on a raised shelf, away from the wet floor near the inlet. The air is cooler than outside, and falling drops echo against the stone. A dry ledge beside the entrance gives room to rest a bag or wait while water is drawn. The basin occupies the centre of the chamber, so movement follows the walls and the containers must be kept within reach.

proposals.label: Raised-house cooking room
proposals.imageDirection: The interior of a raised jungle dwelling, with a broad palm-thatch roof, sturdy dark beams and a low clay hearth set safely on a stone pad. Cooking pots, leaf-wrapped parcels, hanging fruit baskets and covered grain jars surround a smooth timber table. Open shutters admit bright green light from enormous leaves and vines; the wet ground lies visibly below the threshold steps. Warm firelight and red-brown clay contrast with the emerald jungle, emphasizing cooking, shared shelter and practical adaptation to heavy rain.

Jungle sounds arrive through the shutters, mixed with the quiet scrape of mats and the smell of warm clay and cooking food.

proposals.label: Alpaca packing pen
proposals.imageDirection: A shaded alpaca packing enclosure against Vol’dun’s warm red-brown rock, with low dry-stone walls and a patched striped canopy held by salvaged poles. Padded pack saddles, bright woven blankets, rope halters and balanced baskets hang in orderly pairs beside a water trough. Pale-gold dunes and bare twisted desert trees are visible beyond the fence. A small grooming shelf holds combs, hoof tools and covered feed jars; broad mats provide a clean surface for loading bundles. Use clever vulpera salvage and saturated teal, orange and magenta cloth to give the harsh desert a lively practical domestic edge.
proposals.context: Pack saddles and paired baskets hang beneath the shade canopy. A trough occupies the coolest corner, with covered feed jars kept clear of blown sand. A low wall gives visitors somewhere to sit while straps are checked. Open space beside the gate allows animals and loaded packs to move through without passing between the resting places.

proposals.label: Patchcloth and pack room
proposals.imageDirection: A bright vulpera textile room under a shaded rock overhang, enclosed with stitched hide and mismatched turquoise, crimson and yellow cloth. A low loom, folded awnings, packs and cleverly reused sail scraps surround a wide mending mat. Poles, bone needles, metal buckles and recovered buttons hang on a rack assembled from salvaged wood. Through the opening, pale dunes roll toward rugged brown stone and skeletal desert trees. A small lamp and covered water cup occupy a sturdy crate desk. Emphasize nimble adaptation, portable domestic life and colourful resourcefulness, with carefully repaired belongings arranged for reliable everyday use.
proposals.context: Cloth pieces are sorted by strength and size beside the low loom. Packs, awnings and stitched covers lie folded around the mending mat, while needles and buckles remain in divided boxes. The enclosure screens the work from direct sun and much of the drifting sand. A crate desk offers a place to examine a strap, write or set down a cup. The soft cloth walls admit nearby sounds, and almost every item in the room can be packed for transport.
proposals.availability: Vol’dun; active vulpera or compatible salvage-textile household with an accessible mending room or installed caravan workspace. Require actual local community fittings and supplies; the room does not appear merely because a traveller is vulpera.

proposals.label: Beast harness and care hall

A clear raised bench gives visitors space to sit or inspect a strap while remaining outside the lanes used for moving large animals.

Bright turquoise pigment bowls and vermilion cloth add saturated colour beside dark wooden storage chests. proposals.label: Raised fish-smoking room
proposals.imageDirection: A Nazmir fish-preservation hut raised on sturdy dark posts above shallow marsh water. Reed screens shelter racks of fish, covered salt crocks and a low clay smoking hearth standing on a thick stone pad. Hanging moss and immense tree roots crowd around the exterior, seen through a wide doorway in blue-grey wetland mist. Open rolls dry on latticed frames beside carefully shielded lamps; a covered tea vessel and leaf-lined snack bowl sit at the desk. The windows frame immense mossy roots and blue-green wetland mist. Use warm parchment, dark wood, muted shell colours and small turquoise accents. The room should feel patient, well travelled and intensely protective of written memories in a humid landscape.
proposals.context: Scroll cases stand above the floor, with their contents arranged on drying frames or held flat under smooth weights. Covered trays protect blank parchment from wet air. A visitor can examine a text at the desk without entering the storage corner; damp hands and travelling gear have their own place near the door.

proposals.label: Dinosaur harness store
proposals.imageDirection: A reinforced island beast-handling shelter beside rough grey rock, with enormous harnesses hanging from thick timber hooks. Bronze buckles, padded collars and heavy woven ropes occupy a raised preparation deck, separated by a stout rail from a broad feeding enclosure. Tall old conifers and dense green ferns rise behind the roof; island mist softens the mountain slope. Large wash troughs, brush racks and deep fodder baskets establish the practical care of huge scaled animals. Use Zandalari geometric straps sparingly on functional gear, emphasizing bulk, reinforced construction and a clear sheltered place for human-scale conversation.
proposals.context: Harnesses hang from hooks above the preparation deck. Heavy buckles and padded collars are sorted beside brushes, rope and covered feed baskets. A sturdy rail separates this dry area from the broad enclosure beyond. Mist reaches the roof edge, and the wooden floor smells of damp fibre and stored fodder. There is space to examine a strap or discuss its fit without entering the handling lane; carrying the larger harnesses requires the deck to be kept clear.
proposals.availability: Isle of Giants; actual functioning dinosaur-handling facility with the depicted equipment and permitted safe access. Animal presence requires resident managed beasts, not wild island spawn alone. Zandalari fittings require actual current or retained use. proposals.label: Fossil-sheltered hatchery
proposals.imageDirection: A quiet hatchery shelter near warm island rock, where huge pale fossil arches form a canopy above deep baskets of nesting fibre and carefully spaced eggs. Dark timber windbreaks and stone-weighted curtains enclose the sheltered side; a small monitoring table holds shell fragments, soft cloth, water bowls and marked clay tiles. Ancient conifers, giant ferns and grey volcanic slopes remain visible through the opening. Warm stone and amber lamps contrast with cool coastal mist. The eggs and old bones are the visual centre, showing deliberate caretaking beneath ancestral remains, with close accessible bedding and carefully arranged monitoring tools.
proposals.context: Nesting baskets occupy sheltered hollows below the fossil arches. Curtains and low windbreaks steady the air, while shell fragments and soft cloths lie on the monitoring table. The stone retains gentle warmth beneath the floor mats. A quiet bench near the entrance offers somewhere to wait or write without crowding the nests. Large pale bones make the room feel enclosed even where it opens to mist, and tools are set down carefully to avoid disturbing the prepared bedding.

proposals.label: Field specimen cabin
proposals.imageDirection: A naturalist’s small island cabin built from weathered timber beside a grey rock outcrop. Bone fragments, enormous scale samples, feather bundles and labelled stone specimens cover shallow trays on a broad workbench. A clean writing corner holds calipers, waxed notebooks and a magnifying lens; shelves support wicker field baskets and wrapped instruments. Through a deep window appear primeval conifers, luminous green ferns and mist curling over the slope. A stove and two plain chairs lend shelter from the damp. Let the proportions of specimens hint at the island’s gigantic fauna while the room remains convincingly human-scale.
proposals.context: Collected fragments lie in divided trays, separated from the notebooks and clean measuring tools. Large scales and bones occupy the strongest shelves, while wrapped field instruments hang near the door. The stove warms two chairs without heating the specimen corner too strongly. Outside mist beads on the window frame. A broad clear bench provides space to compare a fragment, make a drawing or discuss observations, with baskets ready for carrying material back to the shelves.
proposals.availability: Isle of Giants; actual occupied field-study cabin or comparable specimen facility with permitted access and locally gathered material. Require appropriate instruments for depicted technology. No all-knowing researcher, dangerous live specimen or discovery event is automatic.

proposals.label: Cartel private lounge
proposals.imageDirection: An extravagantly gaudy Kezan private lounge above an industrial business: emerald velvet upholstery, red lacquer, brass pipework and gold-painted mouldings crowd beneath an oversized illuminated profit board. A padded sofa faces a low table piled with contract folders, expensive drink bottles and gaudy snack dishes. A polished safe occupies one wall beside a mechanical serving hatch and ostentatious trophy merchandise. Wide windows show palms, smoking factory stacks and dense green-copper roofs. Make the room aggressively commercial, luxurious and faintly ridiculous, with wealth spent on visible status, ridiculous ornament and clever conveniences packed into every available corner.
proposals.context: The lounge is quiet enough for private conversation despite the distant factory noise. Contracts and drinks share the low table, while a serving hatch keeps refreshments close to the seating. The sofa is heavily padded, and brass fittings retain a faint smell of warm machinery. A locked safe occupies the inner wall. The large windows overlook roofs and smoke; their thick shutters can close for privacy. Any papers laid out here must compete with the room’s conspicuous comforts and crowded decorative surfaces.
proposals.availability: Kezan; intact occupied goblin cartel or compatible commercial building with a private lounge and granted entry. Require its actual wealth and industrial surroundings. Do not select after local destruction unless rebuilt; display boards and powered conveniences require operating technology. No named trade prince or mandatory deal.

proposals.label: Kaja’Cola canning room
proposals.imageDirection: A noisy Kezan canning room with absurdly bright advertising panels, emerald cans with cartoon-weasel labels and a snaking brass conveyor beneath green-painted pressure tanks. Small sealed hoppers and measuring vessels handle glittering mineral additives above a counter stacked with sample cups and prototype labels and bold trademark signs. Riveted metal, hazard stripes and oversized valve wheels make the engineering feel reckless yet profitably organised. A viewing window shows palms through yellow industrial haze. Crates are stamped with loud commercial graphics; a padded sales stool stands beside the tasting counter. Emphasize frenetic goblin consumer spectacle, dense machinery and the pursuit of the next irresistible product.
proposals.context: Cans move through a line of filling nozzles and sealing arms. The machinery gives the room a steady clatter, punctuated by steam from the pressure valves. Sample cups and unused labels sit on a separate counter away from the moving belt. Crates occupy the cleared floor beside the exit. Sweet syrup and warm metal dominate the air. A stool by the tasting surface allows discussion of a batch or its packaging, though voices must rise when the line is running.
proposals.availability: Kezan; operating Kaja’Cola or explicitly compatible kajamite beverage-production site with appropriate industrial technology and visitor access. Require actual mineral/additive supply and power. Product effects must come from current lore/game state, not this room text. Intact or rebuilt site only; no automatic eruption or named franchise.

proposals.label: Prototype blast-test room
proposals.imageDirection: A goblin prototype-testing bunker cut into Kezan’s dark volcanic stone. Thick scarred walls shelter a small observation desk behind broad green-tinted reinforced glass; beyond it stands a battered test cradle surrounded by replaceable armour plates. Unfinished rocket-shaped devices, colourful patent tags, coils of fuse and improbable gadgets crowd secured side cabinets. Brass instruments and oversized red levers gleam under yellow work lights. An emergency door and concrete rubble bins are part of the practical layout. Make the design loudly ambitious, commercially theatrical and visibly accustomed to violent testing, with absurd apparatus kept behind substantial protective barriers.
proposals.context: A reinforced pane divides the observation desk from the scarred testing chamber. Instruments and a padded stool occupy the protected side, while replaceable plates and a holding cradle define the far room. Patent tags and unfinished components are stored in locked cabinets rather than on the seating area. The air smells of scorched metal and stone dust. A broad clear desk allows diagrams to be examined or discussed, and the side door keeps entry separate from the chamber’s heavy access gate.
proposals.availability: Kezan; intact or rebuilt goblin experimental facility with a maintained blast-testing chamber, working protections and permitted access. Require actual relevant technology and stored prototypes. No live test, explosion, injury or character appetite for danger is imposed.

proposals.label: Bamboo-house cookroom
proposals.imageDirection: A tropical domestic cookroom built with stout bamboo framing, woven reed walls and a deep palm-thatch roof. A low clay hearth supports a blackened pot beside baskets of fruit, wrapped fish and broad leaves prepared for serving. Bright daylight enters through the doorway, revealing thick bamboo, palms and humid jungle over volcanic ground. Wooden bowls, fibre mats and a curtained sleeping niche give the room an intimate household scale. Small shells and coloured cloth brighten the green-brown palette. Emphasize the Lost Isles’ lush new-growth vegetation, plentiful natural materials and warmth, with shelter from sudden tropical rain.
proposals.context: The cookroom is shaded beneath a deep thatched roof. Fruit baskets and leaf-wrapped food hang above the floor, while bowls and a covered pot sit beside the low hearth. The doorway admits bamboo shadows and damp jungle air. A mat offers room for a meal or quiet conversation without crowding the cooking corner. The sleeping niche is screened from the main table, and wet clothing can be left by the entrance rather than over the household’s stored food.
proposals.availability: Lost Isles; occupied dwelling using bamboo-and-thatch domestic construction, with an accessible cooking room and local provisions. Require actual current settlement and entry. Native pygmy-specific ornaments need the relevant culture; no forced goblin shipwreck, refugee arrival or volcanic event.

proposals.label: Kajamite assay room
proposals.imageDirection: A small mineral-assay room at a Lost Isles extraction site, with dark volcanic stone footings, a patched roof and an orderly crushing bench. Greenish mineral fragments occupy divided trays beside balance scales, a mortar, sealed sample jars and protective cloth wraps. A locked dry cabinet stands opposite an open shutter framing dense bamboo and bright palms. Warm lamps illuminate chiselled stone and reused metal fittings; a rough chair sits at the clear notes counter. Keep the facility local and improvised, combining the tropical island’s rugged resources with careful measurement, makeshift furnishings and compact hand-operated tools.

Balance weights, a mortar and closed jars occupy a clean shelf, and the notes counter stays clear of grit. Jungle air enters through the shutter above the dark stone sill. A chair allows close discussion of samples without standing beside the tools. Cloth wraps contain material ready for carrying, while the locked cabinet keeps completed samples apart from incoming stone and everyday supplies.

proposals.label: Island fish-preserving house
proposals.imageDirection: An airy Lost Isles food-preservation house near the coast, raised on short poles above sandy volcanic ground. Bamboo rails carry salt-curing fish and drying sea greens under a broad thatched roof; shallow clay pans, shellfish baskets and covered jars line a woven wall. Through the open side, palms lean over golden sand, dark shoreline stone and brilliantly blue water. Red-orange coals warm a little clay stove at the clean end, beside a low eating bench. Use dense tropical green against sunlit sand and black rock, with handmade domestic objects expressing resourceful ordinary coastal life.
proposals.context: Fish dry beneath the roof where the breeze can reach them. Shellfish baskets and covered jars stand beside the washing pans, while the little stove warms the room’s clean end. Salt and cooking smoke mingle with the damp smell of sea greens. A low bench gives room for a meal or a conversation while provisions are wrapped. Wet material drains over the sandy ground, separate from the dry baskets kept inside, and the broad roof shelters everything from sudden rain.
proposals.availability: Lost Isles; occupied coastal settlement with functioning food-preservation facilities and edible local marine resources. Require a safe accessible building. Foods follow actual catches; no named refugee camp, compulsory mackerel catch or current eruption.

proposals.label: Hill cistern room
proposals.imageDirection: A cool water-storage chamber built into a Glaive Isle hillside of weathered stone. A covered basin collects runoff from an uphill channel, surrounded by clay water jars, a wooden bucket shelf and a broad dry ledge. One deep opening frames the island’s rolling green slopes, pale coastal rock and blue sea below. Rough masonry and sturdy beams give the room a modest settled-island character. Warm reflected light at the entrance fades into blue-grey shade around the basin. Keep the architecture confidently practical and land-based, with its shape determined by sloping ground, thick retaining walls and cool water storage.
proposals.context: The basin sits in the cool inner part of the hillside chamber. Water jars occupy raised shelves, while a bucket and measuring cup rest on the dry ledge. Drops echo softly beneath the beams. The entrance looks down the slope toward the sea and brings in enough light to check a container. A bench offers space to wait or talk while keeping travelling gear off the wet floor, and the narrow channel makes the source of incoming water easy to trace.
proposals.availability: Glaive Isle; an actual maintained hill cistern in an inhabited location with a usable water source and access. Match current local builders and household fittings. No invented glaive cult, night-elven occupation, inland magic or underwater terrain.

Tools can be laid out near the garden doorway, while the curtained storage corner keeps dry food and personal belongings away from rain reaching the outer threshold.

Through the shutter appear rolling green hills, pale coastal rock and blue water. A covered fuel bin, floor drain and clean bench for visitors make the workplace practical. proposals.label: Banana ripening house
proposals.imageDirection: A broad Tel Abim fruit house beneath a deep palm-thatch roof, its slatted timber walls lined with hanging banana bunches in different stages of ripeness. Yellow fruit dominates the palette against dark wood and emerald leaves; a bench at the clean end holds tasting bowls and a covered drink jar. proposals.label: Leaf-fibre packing room

Clay dye bowls and shells provide small warm accents. A low table and clear mat form the human-scale centre, emphasizing the practical richness of plant materials, close handwork and a household’s well-used carrying equipment.

proposals.label: Mask and drum craft room
proposals.imageDirection: A Darkspear household craft room beneath a steep hide-and-thatch roof, with thick timber posts, woven walls and a raised dry floor. Carved masks in turquoise, red and yellow hang beside drum frames, hide strips and patterned bead cords. A broad low bench holds pigments, small carving blades and binding fibre; finished drums rest beyond the clean seating mat. The doorway reveals rain-dark rock, wet bright grass and dense island woodland. Warm lamp light catches bold carved faces and leather textures. Keep the design expressive and tactile, rooted in Darkspear craft and communal performance, visible handwork and close household-scale storage.
proposals.context: Masks hang above the low craft bench, with pigments and carving tools kept in separate bowls. Drum frames and prepared hides occupy the dry end of the room. The raised floor shelters everything from wet ground, and rain can be heard against the roof. A clear mat gives visitors room to sit while a carving or binding is examined. Bead cords and loose fibre stay in covered baskets; the unfinished pieces are close enough for their textures and workmanship to be seen.

proposals.label: Rainproof guest hearth
proposals.imageDirection: A sturdy Darkspear-style domestic guest room built around a low stone hearth and thick rounded timber supports. Layered woven mats, hide curtains and bright patterned cloth divide sleeping spaces beneath a steep roof. Bowls, a covered water jar and wrapped food rest on a low shelf; a drying rail holds spare cloaks and blankets. Through the doorway appear wet green woodland, grey rock and rain-bright grass beneath overlapping dark green branches. Amber embers illuminate turquoise-red textiles and dark wood. Give the room a sheltering communal warmth shaped by heavy island weather and practical household hospitality.
proposals.context: The hearth warms a central circle of woven mats, with sleeping places screened along the room’s sides. Spare cloth and blankets hang above the driest shelf. Bowls and a covered water jar are close enough for a simple meal, while dripping clothing belongs near the entrance. Rain beats on the steep roof and drains beyond the threshold. The shared arrangement offers room for quiet conversation or rest, though curtains soften light more readily than the sounds of nearby movement.

proposals.label: Coastal records room
proposals.imageDirection: A land-based Balor administrative room of old pale stone and heavy ship-timber beams. A broad desk holds coastal charts, shipping rolls, sealed letters and brass weights beside narrow cupboards of bound records. Deep shutters frame grassy island ground, rocky shore and open blue-grey water. A small hearth and plain chairs make the chamber serviceable in sea weather; iron brackets, wax seals and worn floorboards communicate long naval use. Keep the room modest and civic, with practical storage, durable chairs, an accessible consultation table and restrained coastal craftsmanship.
proposals.context: Charts and records occupy the desk and narrow wall cupboards. Sealed packets remain in divided trays, while brass weights hold open pages against drafts from the shutters. The hearth warms the chairs nearest the table. Sea weather is visible through the deep window but softened by the stone walls. The room provides space to compare routes, inspect a document or write privately, with dry storage close at hand and the entrance passage separate from the working surface.
proposals.availability: Balor; an actual maintained land-based civic or naval records room in an inhabited settlement, with appropriate access. Records and seals belong to the current polity. Native GoA2 Balor does not imply modern underwater Vashj’ir, naga rule or active Stormreaver occupation.

A small shutter admits pale daylight from grass and coastal rock above the steps; sea damp has darkened the outer threshold. Measuring scoops, a hanging scale and a rough inventory board occupy a clear counter. Use weathered grey stone, warm grain colours and restrained ironwork, emphasizing dependable island food storage at ordinary household or communal scale.

A dry ledge gives room to set down bags, compare containers or discuss provisions; larger sacks go up the narrow steps one at a time.

proposals.label: Yak Grooming Shelter
proposals.imageDirection: A Kun-Lai yak-care shelter built around a broad shallow wash channel in the golden foothills. Massive shaggy yaks stand at long timber rails beneath a heavy curved thatched roof; brushes, wooden combs, drying blankets, broad leather harnesses, and padded pack saddles occupy clearly separated bays. The mountainous setting appears through the open end: ochre grass, grey boulders, sparse trees, and a distant wall of snow-dark peaks. Include a fenced drying yard, fresh-water buckets, and a small raised measuring bench. Let the animals' bulk and dense fur make ordinary equipment feel unusually stout.
proposals.context: Wet wool and clean water scent the grooming shelter. Broad brushes rest beside the wash channel, while drying blankets and padded harnesses hang beyond the spray. The rails leave enough room for a yak's immense shoulders and shaggy coat; the raised bench holds smaller straps and measures clear of muddy hooves. A visitor can inspect tack from the dry bay or approach the animal rail more closely. Mountain air moves through the open end, carrying the sound of water into the shelter.
proposals.availability: Kun-Lai Summit membership; a yak ranch, caravan animal-care station, or household with trained pack yaks. Prefer inhabited golden foothills rather than bare high snowfields. Animal approach requires keeper access.

proposals.label: Mountain Scroll-Copying Room
proposals.imageDirection: An intimate Kun-Lai scholarly chamber in a thick-walled hill institution, with red timber brackets, grey stone walls, and a steep glazed roof visible through a high window. Long scroll cases and cloth-wrapped books line deep shelves; individual low desks hold inkstones, broad brushes, weights, and drying sheets. A brazier gives a restrained warmth below a hanging vent. Snow-bright mountains and a blossoming courtyard tree appear in the window's narrow view. Show a clean central examination table and an inner screened desk, emphasizing handwork, careful preservation, and substantial mountain construction rather than a grand library landmark.
proposals.context: Ink and warmed wood lend the chamber a dry, quiet smell. Scroll weights keep unfurled pages steady beneath the high window, and the shelves' cloth wrappings protect older works from mountain dust. The central table is clear enough to examine a document together; the screened desk beyond it offers a more secluded place for correspondence. Thick walls soften the institution's outside sounds. Only the brazier's low crackle and the occasional brush against paper break the room's stillness.
proposals.availability: Kun-Lai Summit membership; a literate household, monastery, archive, or scholar's workplace. Access to works and the inner desk depends on the institution and character permissions.

New use: Private scholarship, copying, and document examination, distinct from the first-pass training guest court.

proposals.label: Family Remembrance Terrace
proposals.imageDirection: A modest Kun-Lai remembrance terrace cut into a grey foothill slope above golden grass. Weathered grave markers and small upright name tablets stand beneath a curved timber shelter, with stone offering ledges, lidded incense vessels, and a basin for washing hands. The forms are sturdy and warmly Pandarian: red-painted braces, simple cloud carvings, and carefully swept pale paving. A dwarf pine bends over the enclosure, with snow mountains immense beyond its low wall. Set a sheltered bench beside the entry, leaving generous clear space before the family markers rather than reproducing a royal tomb.
proposals.context: The terrace holds the cool scent of stone and the lingering sweetness of incense. Its markers stand close enough to read from the swept paving, with offering ledges and washing water within easy reach. The entry bench gives visitors a place to wait while the space before the tablets remains open. Wind stirs the pine above the shelter and exposes the vast mountain view beyond the low wall. The enclosure is small enough for remembrance to remain a family matter.
proposals.availability: Kun-Lai Summit membership; a resident household or community whose burial and remembrance practice supports tablets, offerings, and incense. Gate lit incense and offerings to actual use; access follows the custodians' customs.

proposals.label: Mobile Yaungol Oil Works
proposals.imageDirection: A mobile Yaungol oil-working installation on Townlong's wind-swept green steppe: a squat, powerful timber derrick on a heavy movable base, horn-tipped braces, blackened pump fittings, and iron-bound oil vessels laid out on absorbent gravel. Ox-sized carrying yokes and thick leather hoses show equipment made for massive bodies. Separate the filling station from a guarded firepit by a broad cleared strip. Small russet trees and immense pale cliffs rise beyond a simple hide windbreak. The contraption should look rough, ingenious, transportable, and capable of bringing combustible earth into a nomadic camp's daily work.
proposals.context: Heavy oil leaves a dark sheen around the pump fittings and a sharp smell in the wind. Thick hoses lead to iron-bound vessels on the gravel filling pad; a cleared strip separates them from the firepit. The derrick's wheels and detachable braces reveal how much of the installation can be moved. A hide windbreak shelters the measuring shelf and repair tools, offering a place for practical negotiation within sight of the work while keeping visitors out of the fuel-handling lane.
proposals.availability: Townlong Steppes membership; active Yaungol or inherited Yaungol-style oil extraction with an actual resource site. Open flame, fuel quantity, and facility access depend on current operation. Not a generic feature of every camp.

proposals.label: Steppe Burial Enclosure
proposals.imageDirection: A Yaungol burial enclosure on a sheltered Townlong hillside, defined by stout horn-topped timber stakes and low earthen graves covered with carefully weighted stone. Tough hides protect small remembrance ledges from the wind; carved markers and lidded ritual vessels cluster beneath a massive russet-leaved tree. Oversized footprints, broad hand tools, and a high washing bowl communicate the scale of the custodians. Deep green grass and pale stepped cliffs dominate the surrounding landscape. Include a simple outer waiting bench and a narrow inner path between the graves, keeping the composition solemn, material, and intimately local.
proposals.context: Wind moves softly through the hide shelter above the graves. Weighted stones hold the earth in place, and carved markers remain close to the narrow inner path. The washing bowl and covered vessels give the custodians a practical place to prepare their work. An outer bench leaves visitors outside the grave enclosure until they are received. Here the steppe's open scale draws back to individual names, small offerings, and the care required to keep a burial place ordered through harsh weather.
proposals.availability: Townlong Steppes membership; a Yaungol burial ground or community maintaining its inherited burial customs. Ritual vessels and active practices must match current faith. Custodian permission gates the inner enclosure.

proposals.label: Wall Beacon Service Gallery
proposals.imageDirection: A maintenance gallery inside the great defensive wall along Townlong's eastern edge, emphasizing the human-scale work beneath its colossal Pandarian masonry. Thick grey blocks, cloud-carved brackets, steep red-and-teal roofwork, and narrow viewing slits frame a sheltered service bay. Oil-free lamp stores, bundled beacon fuel, spare winch ropes, ladder sections, and stone repair pieces sit in orderly racks. A short stair rises toward an ordinary beacon platform, while a dry worktable holds section diagrams and fitted replacement parts. A window shows green steppe and a far pale cliff, making the immense structure's everyday upkeep tangible.
proposals.context: Cool masonry encloses the gallery, with the steppe wind audible through narrow slits. Coiled ropes, fitted repair stones, and neatly bundled fuel leave only a clear service lane between the racks. The worktable holds diagrams of neighboring wall sections, and a short stair gives access to the beacon above. Its thick door and inward-facing bench allow a practical discussion sheltered from the exposed walkway. Even at rest, the stored ladders and winch parts reveal the labor that keeps this vast barrier usable.
proposals.availability: Only Townlong counties or baronies adjoining an actual Serpent's Spine segment or maintained derivative defensive wall; do not expose throughout the region. Active beacon stores and staffing depend on current maintenance. Service access required.

proposals.label: Kypari Sap Brewroom
proposals.imageDirection: A compact Pandaren brewroom at a sheltered edge of the Dread Wastes, its heavy timber and woven roof tucked beneath a huge twisted kypari root. Filtered orange sap runs from sealed ceramic jars into a small copper kettle; tasting cups, annotated mixing sticks, and cloudy fermenting vessels occupy a separate clean bench. Outside the shutters, blue-violet plants and black tree limbs surround a luminous amber seam. Curved red wooden brackets and a neatly kept tea corner bring domestic warmth into an alien environment. Focus on drink preparation and sampling, with gathering tools stored away from the brewing floor.
proposals.context: Warm resin sweetness rises from the kettle, sharper and stranger than the grain scents of an ordinary brew house. Sealed sap jars stand above cloudy fermenting vessels, while marked stirring sticks and tasting cups occupy the clean bench. The shutters give the room a controlled view of violet undergrowth and an amber-lit root outside. Two low stools sit beside the notes, close enough to compare a sample or discuss a batch while staying clear of the hot working floor.
proposals.availability: Dread Wastes membership; an established sap-brewing household or institution with safely usable kypari ingredients. Gate to actual occupation and functioning production; changes to local contamination require a compatible variant.

proposals.label: Amber Scorpion Care Ring
proposals.imageDirection: An enclosed handling ring for a trained amber scorpion in the Dread Wastes. The creature has a heavy, translucent amber-colored carapace and articulated dark joints; padded restraints, long grooming implements, reinforced feed containers, and an oversized saddle show practical care for a dangerous mount. Faceted resin partitions and dark rootlike structural ribs make the enclosure recognizably Mantid rather than a human stable. Pale blue-violet ground plants catch amber light through a high vent. Compose an outer inspection platform behind a sturdy barrier, with the keeper's inner working space clearly separated from the animal's turning circle.
proposals.context: Hard claws click against the ring's floor, and warm amber light passes through the scorpion's heavy plates. Long brushes and padded tack hang behind the inner barrier, beyond the creature's turning space. The outer platform offers a close view of the animal and its saddle without opening the handling gate. Feed vessels and repair straps occupy a sheltered keeper's bay, where practical conversation remains possible over the scrape of articulated legs. Every partition gives care and observation their own distance.
proposals.availability: Dread Wastes membership; an actual trained amber scorpion and a maintained care facility. Access to the inner ring requires a suitable handler and permission; replace live-animal detail if the ring is unoccupied.

proposals.label: Mantid Sonic Workroom
proposals.imageDirection: An intimate Mantid instrument workroom built from dark chitinous structural curves and angular amber-lit recesses. Small resonating devices, suspended plates, ribbed tubes, and carefully fitted amber communication components occupy several standing benches scaled to insectoid bodies. Hanging test pieces are isolated within their own alcoves; fine tools and diagrams emphasize repair and tuning rather than a giant weapon. A screened service recess and quiet outer ledge provide places for examining finished components. Beyond a narrow vent loom immense kypari roots and violet foliage. Let faceted glow and precise alien geometry dominate the palette.
proposals.context: Fine vibrations travel through the bench supports, accompanied by thin clicks and tones at the edge of ordinary hearing. Fitted communication pieces sit beside spare plates, each set apart from the suspended test instruments. Amber recesses light the room without flattening its deep, insectile curves. An outer ledge accommodates inspection and exchange; the inner alcoves contain the exacting work of tuning. Its sounds make the space feel busy even between visible movements, while a screened recess shelters delicate parts from accidental contact.
proposals.availability: Dread Wastes membership; an operating Mantid sonic communication or instrument-maintenance facility. Active test sounds require suitable Mantid equipment and users. Access and a non-Mantid visitor's hearing or comprehension limits remain character-specific.

proposals.label: Scroll Restoration Room
proposals.imageDirection: A refined Vale chamber for repairing and preserving old written works. Golden foliage casts warm light through a large carved lattice window, behind which pale sheer cliffs rise over flowering gardens. Red-lacquered shelves hold cloth-covered scroll cases; a broad low table displays weighted papers, soft brushes, backing sheets, and ceramic paste pots. Covered warming trays and a drying frame occupy the working side. Teal roof tiles, cloud-pattern brackets, and rich but restrained cushions establish a prosperous Pandarian institution. Divide the clean examination seating from the delicate restoration bench with a low openwork screen.
proposals.context: The room smells of paper, paste, and gently warmed wood. A sheet lies flat beneath smooth weights, its damaged edge supported by a fresh backing; covered scroll cases stand above the drying frame. Golden leaves filter the window light across the clean examination table. Cushions on its outer side give visitors a place to consult a work without crowding the repair bench. The low screen preserves a clear working boundary while leaving enough sight and sound for an unhurried scholarly exchange.
proposals.availability: Vale of Eternal Blossoms membership; an intact archive, literate household, or lore-preserving institution. Match the Vale's current environmental condition; access to particular texts follows their custody.

proposals.label: Blossom-View Dressing Chamber
proposals.imageDirection: A private upper room in an affluent Vale residence, with polished red timber, dark lacquer chests, embroidered folding screens, and a broad mirror in a carved cloud frame. Hanging robes and layered sashes emphasize exquisite Pandarian silk, with gold and jade ornaments laid on a small padded table. The open balcony frames golden-leaved trees, luminous blossoms, and pale precipitous cliffs. A deep teal roof overhang shields the room from direct sun. Arrange an outer sitting cushion and a screened inner dressing area so the scene expresses household refinement, preparation, and degrees of intimacy rather than a ruler's public audience.
proposals.context: Soft silk hangs beside lacquer chests, and a light floral scent drifts in from the balcony. Sashes and small ornaments wait on a padded table beneath the mirror; the screen shelters the space where clothing is adjusted and stored. The outer cushion offers a place for a close visitor to sit while remaining outside the dressing area. Golden reflected light gives the room a quiet warmth, and its upper-floor position draws conversation away from the household's more public rooms.
proposals.availability: Vale of Eternal Blossoms membership; a prosperous residence with an intact private upper floor. Resident architectural style and household access must support this room; environmental appearance follows current Vale condition.

proposals.label: Blossom Grafting House
proposals.imageDirection: A protected horticultural workhouse beside a Vale garden, with red timber lattice walls, glazed teal eaves, and small stone channels carrying clear water past rows of nursery pots. Golden-leaved saplings and flowering branches fill the space with warm color; grafting knives, ties, trellises, and labeled propagation trays lie on a waist-high bench. Beyond the open side stand mature luminous trees against pale sheer cliffs. Keep the planting intimate and carefully tended rather than a sweeping ceremonial garden. A dry sheltered niche holds pruning diagrams, a clean work apron, and stools for examining a delicate graft.
proposals.context: Moist earth and fresh bark scent the workhouse. Slender ties hold new grafts against their stocks, and shallow channels keep water moving beside the nursery pots. Golden leaves brighten the lattice walls; the smallest flowering plants occupy sheltered trays away from the draft. A dry niche offers stools and a place to compare pruning diagrams with the living branches. The ordered beds make horticulture tangible here, with each tied shoot carrying its own careful work and expectation.
proposals.availability: Vale of Eternal Blossoms membership; an actively tended garden or estate nursery with healthy compatible plants. Corrupted or devastated holdings require an appropriate variant; inner facility access depends on its caretakers.

proposals.label: Tidal Smokehouse
proposals.imageDirection: A Krasarang fish-preserving house on short stout stilts above damp sand and tidal mud, its bamboo lashings and broad curved roof darkened by the humid jungle. Split fish hang from deep rafters over an enclosed low smoking hearth; ceramic salt jars, woven drying screens, and broad cutting boards fill the working side. A vented roof releases a thin plume through immense tropical leaves. The pale shore and jade-blue shallows appear beyond an open hatch. A screened dry annex contains storage chests, a bench, and a tally slate, with no dock or market dominating the view.
proposals.context: Woodsmoke and salt settle into the smokehouse timbers. Hanging fish turn slowly in the warm draft, and a lidded hearth keeps the working heat below the racks. Raised boards divide the cutting floor from the dry annex, where chests and a tally slate record food that can outlast the next tide. Rain ticks on the deep roof and the sea moves beyond the hatch. The screened bench gives a visitor shelter without crossing directly into the food-preparation space.
proposals.availability: Krasarang Wilds membership; a settled fishing community with active preserving facilities. Use compatible shoreline settlement architecture; interior access belongs to the workshop or household.

proposals.label: Jungle Recovery Room
proposals.imageDirection: A small shaded recovery room in a Krasarang dwelling, with a high vented timber roof and woven reed shutters filtering green light from the dense jungle. Broad bamboo-framed couches lie behind cloth screens; ceramic basins, folded clean linens, mortar bowls, and tagged bundles of local gathered plants occupy a practical side table. A covered water pot and raised shelves protect supplies from damp. The architecture is warmly Pandarian, with curved brackets and simple red trim. Compose a quiet receiving seat beside the entrance and deeper resting space beneath the widest awning, open to humid coastal air.
proposals.context: Filtered jungle light rests on clean folded cloth and the rim of a water basin. Crushed leaves lend the room a sharp green scent beneath the heavier smell of rain. Cloth screens give each couch its own sheltered space, and raised shelves keep the supplies above the damp floor. The entrance seat permits a quiet visit or a practical conversation before anyone approaches the resting area. Beyond the shutters, insect calls and falling water make the enclosed room feel especially still.
proposals.availability: Krasarang Wilds membership; an established healer's household, monastery infirmary, or recovery facility. Treatment, patient presence, and religious symbols depend on the actual institution; inner visits require its access rules.

proposals.label: Reed-Mat Weaver's House
proposals.imageDirection: A Krasarang domestic weaving room on a raised timber platform, with bundled marsh reeds drying beneath the curved eaves and a huge glossy-leaved tree shading its open wall. The work is unmistakably wetland craft: split reed strips, fish-basket forms, rolled floor mats, and tightly plaited screens crowd a low working frame. Pale sand, dark jungle roots, and shallow turquoise water remain visible below the platform. Weathered bamboo posts and lacquered red braces frame a household corner with a kettle, sleeping mat, and shuttered personal chest, separated from the coarse fiber work by a finished reed screen.
proposals.context: Fresh reeds smell grassy beside the drying bundles, while older mats retain a faint salt scent. Loose strips spread across the working frame; a half-finished screen shows how tightly the strands can close together. The raised platform catches a little breeze above the wet ground. Image direction: A Krasarang domestic weaving room on a raised timber platform, with bundled marsh reeds drying beneath the curved eaves and a huge glossy-leaved tree shading its open wall. The work is unmistakably wetland craft: split reed strips, fish-basket forms, rolled floor mats, and tightly plaited screens crowd a low working frame. Pale sand, dark jungle roots, and shallow turquoise water remain visible below the platform. Weathered bamboo posts and lacquered red braces frame a household corner with a kettle, sleeping mat, and shuttered personal chest, separated from the coarse fiber work by a finished reed screen.

proposals.label: Greenstone Polishing Room
proposals.imageDirection: A shaded stoneworker's room in the Jade Forest, its open lattice windows framing gigantic bamboo and a pale, moss-topped karst bluff. Deep green stone slabs sit in timber cradles; unfinished bowls, dragon-shaped finials, and small ornamental panels show successive stages of cutting and polish. A treadle-driven polishing wheel stands beside a water trough, with abrasive grit sorted into ceramic jars. Dark red beams and turquoise roof tiles lend quiet Pandaren elegance to a practical, damp workspace. Include a clean sample shelf and two low stools beyond the gritty working floor.
proposals.context: Wet grit darkens the floor around the polishing wheel, and the room smells of damp stone and fresh-cut wood. Rough green blocks become glossy under the window light; finished pieces occupy a clean shelf beside padded carrying cases. The low stools offer a place to discuss commissions while delicate work remains within arm's reach of its benches. A sliding lattice door closes off the dusty cutting room, leaving this smaller chamber well suited to a measured, private exchange.
proposals.availability: Jade Forest membership; a functioning greenstone or ornamental stone workshop. Favor established quarry and artisan districts, especially d_greenstone. Workshop access is required for its inner room.

proposals.label: Cloud Serpent Nursery
proposals.imageDirection: A sheltered cloud-serpent rearing enclosure against a Jade Forest hillside, enclosed by curved wooden rails beneath an immense spreading tree. Oversized woven nests, padded egg cradles, shallow water bowls, and honey-stained feeding implements sit under sweeping teal-tiled awnings. A few long-bodied, brightly scaled young cloud serpents coil through the enclosure, with whiskers and small antlers distinguishing them from ordinary snakes. Bamboo, hanging lanterns, blossom branches, and pale mountain silhouettes establish the region. Put a handwashing basin and a sheltered observation bench outside the inner nursery gate.
proposals.context: Sweet honey and warm straw mingle beneath the nursery awnings. Young cloud serpents have room to curl between their nests and shallow bowls, while padded cradles keep the eggs clear of the busy feeding floor. The outer bench overlooks the enclosure without opening its gate. Washing bowls, soft brushes, and carefully spaced feeding tools make this a place for patient animal care; entering the nursery brings a visitor into a much more intimate working space than observing from the rail.
proposals.availability: Jade Forest membership; an established cloud-serpent breeding or training institution with living young. Gate young and eggs to actual facility contents, and inner access to its keepers' permission.

proposals.label: Bamboo Honey House
proposals.imageDirection: A small domestic honey-processing house at the edge of a Jade Forest orchard, with fat bamboo uprights, pale plaster panels, and a roof that curls upward under blue-green glazed tiles. A screened worktable holds honeycomb frames, broad ceramic catch bowls, reed strainers, and wax cakes; sealed honey jars occupy shelves safely above floor level. Warm amber sunlight enters through slatted shutters, contrasting with the cool jade foliage outside. A timber screen separates the sticky processing bench from a dry family corner furnished with cushions, tea cups, and a covered food basket.
proposals.context: Honey scents the small room, and a trace of wax clings to the comb knives and strainers. The screened table keeps the sticky work contained, while glazed jars line the dry shelves beyond it. Outside, bamboo leaves rustle over the orchard; inside, shutters soften the light enough for a quiet conversation at the family cushions. The woven divider makes a clear boundary between household hospitality and the careful handling of the season's sweet stores.
proposals.availability: Jade Forest membership; a settled apiary, orchard, or honey-producing household. Use with locally compatible settlement architecture and resident household access.

proposals.label: Imperial Relief Workshop
proposals.imageDirection: An enclosed Isle of Thunder carving workshop fitted into massive Mogu masonry. A half-finished relief of stylized warriors and curling storm-cloud patterns rests in a heavy stone cradle; huge chisels, mallets, fine finishing tools, and mineral pigment bowls occupy tiered racks suited to enormous hands. Gold and cobalt architectural bands catch brazier light against rain-dark grey stone. High slit windows show the stormy sky above wet island vegetation. Include a smaller clean sample table for visitors and a shuttered back bay for fragile finishing work, emphasizing imposing imperial design expressed through daily craft.
proposals.context: Stone dust settles on the cradle beneath a half-finished relief. Heavy tools hang above finer chisels and pigment bowls, showing the difference between rough shaping and the final painted edge. Braziers warm the gold and blue bands along the workshop walls while rain murmurs at the high windows. The clean sample table offers a place to examine a design without crossing the cutting floor; behind its shutter, the finishing bay provides a quieter, more restricted space for delicate work.
proposals.availability: Isle of Thunder membership; a maintained workshop working in Mogu monumental stonecraft, whether original or inherited. Active braziers and commissions depend on present operation; workshop access required.

proposals.label: Stormwater Cistern Gallery
proposals.imageDirection: A vaulted service gallery beneath an Isle of Thunder holding, where monumental grey stone supports deep rainwater cisterns. Massive square pillars bear worn gold-and-blue Mogu bands; carved channels descend from roof drains into settling basins and overflow gates. Broad cleaning brushes, long-handled strainers, fitted sluice slabs, and waterproof storage pots line a dry maintenance ledge. Light enters through small grates, with reflected water rippling across the vault. A protected inspection table and clear crossing slabs make the space usable for routine service, while its scale retains the island's immense imperial architecture.
proposals.context: Water drops echo through the vault and collect in dark settling pools. Roof channels feed the nearest basin, while fitted gates lead overflow toward a deeper passage. Long brushes and strainers rest above the wet line on the maintenance ledge. Reflections move across the old gold-and-blue pillar bands. The dry inspection table permits a practical conversation beside the water system, but beyond the crossing slabs the gallery narrows into service spaces where the depth and steady current demand closer attention.
proposals.availability: Isle of Thunder membership; an accessible holding with maintained rainwater collection and cistern infrastructure. Water level and gate operation must fit actual conditions; service-gallery access required.

proposals.label: Ancestral Tablet Chamber
proposals.imageDirection: A small ancestral memorial chamber within the Isle of Thunder's colossal stone architecture. Upright carved name slabs sit in deep wall niches beneath severe Mogu relief faces; offering shelves, lidded incense vessels, and tall oil lamps establish a tended ritual space. Cobalt pigment and narrow gold borders accent grey stone without softening its monumental weight. A high opening admits the cold light of rain, while a thick screen wall conceals the inner memorial alcoves from the entrance. Include a simple washing basin and an outer stone seat, keeping the scene intimate rather than reproducing a royal graveyard.
proposals.context: Cold stone and lingering incense scent the memorial chamber. Name slabs stand deep within the wall, with low offering shelves and tall lamps beside them. The entrance seat faces a washing basin, while a thick screen blocks a direct view into the inner alcoves. Rainlight reaches only the nearest carved face. The room gives remembrance distinct stages of approach: the outer waiting space, the sheltered passage, and the close stone recess where a name and its offerings can be attended privately.
proposals.availability: Isle of Thunder membership; an actual Mogu or inherited ancestral memorial whose current custodians retain compatible practices. Ritual contents and lit vessels follow current faith and use; inner admission follows memorial customs.

proposals.label: Giant Vegetable Cellar
proposals.imageDirection: The deep, cool storage cellar of a prosperous Valley of the Four Winds farmhouse. Enormous pumpkins and gourds dwarf ordinary baskets, with thick ropes helping hold them in timber racks; radishes and cabbages hang or rest in compartments sized for Pandaria's exuberant harvests. Low stone retaining walls, heavy beams, packed earth, and round ceramic preserving crocks create a sturdy rural interior. A high ventilation shaft admits a wedge of golden daylight from the orchard above. Show a broad descending stair, a weighing bench, and a small dry shelf for household records and lamps.
proposals.context: Cool earth and pickled vegetables scent the cellar. The harvest's immense size is easiest to grasp here: one pumpkin occupies a whole rack, and thick ropes steady the stored gourds above rows of preserving crocks. The broad stair leads back to the household kitchen; a weighing bench leaves room to inspect stores or settle a practical matter away from the farm's public bustle. Low beams and carefully stacked food make movement deliberate, especially between the deepest shelves.
proposals.availability: Valley of the Four Winds membership; a working farm household with a substantial harvest cellar. Domestic access required.

proposals.label: Irrigation Gatehouse
proposals.imageDirection: A compact irrigation service house spanning a branching farm channel in the Valley of the Four Winds. Its stout timber frame, straw roof, and curved eaves shelter wooden sluice levers, a geared waterwheel axle, and racks of replacement boards. The channel passes beneath the floor, visible through a service opening; outside, terraced green plots and gigantic vegetables climb toward honey-colored trees. Concentrate the view on the mechanism, wet stone channel walls, pegged repair pieces, and a dry raised inspection platform. Keep the setting small, ingenious, and deeply agricultural rather than industrially metallic.
proposals.context: Water presses steadily beneath the gatehouse floor, turning the axle with a slow wooden knock. Worn levers control the branching channels, and spare sluice boards are marked to fit their different widths. A raised platform keeps ledgers and visitors clear of the wet service opening. Conversations carry over the current here, but the enclosed room puts the practical business of shared water within sight and reach: every adjustment sends a visible change into the cultivated fields beyond.
proposals.availability: Valley of the Four Winds membership; maintained farm irrigation infrastructure. Working wheel and flowing channels require an active water supply.

proposals.label: Silkworm Rearing Loft
proposals.imageDirection: A spacious loft in a Valley silk-producing household, with shallow leaf-lined rearing trays supporting unusually large Pandarian silkworms. Timber partitions divide feeding trays, cocoon racks, and a bright winding bench; skeins of white, cream, and lustrous pale-gold thread hang clear of the floor. Rounded beams and broad thatched eaves keep the agricultural architecture warm and substantial. Through an open shutter lie fertile green fields and yellow-leaved trees. Show baskets of fresh feed, fine combs, thread spindles, and a clean curtained fitting alcove, emphasizing attentive cultivation and skilled textile work.
proposals.context: Leaves whisper under the silkworms, and fresh feed lends the warm loft a green, slightly sweet smell. Trays and cocoon racks separate the animals' care from the clean winding bench, where pale threads catch the window light. Hanging skeins leave narrow passages through the work. A curtained fitting alcove offers privacy for examining cloth or taking measurements, while the open bench suits discussion of texture, quality, and the time a fine piece will take to finish.
proposals.availability: Valley of the Four Winds membership; a functioning silk farm or silk-working household. Living worms require an active rearing operation.

proposals.label: Mountain Spring Bath
proposals.imageDirection: A small hot-spring bathing enclosure on the Veiled Stair, pressed between steep grey rock and the roots of a pale-barked mountain tree. Mineral-stained stone forms a broad natural pool, with rising steam drifting beneath a curved timber shelter. Reed screens, folded towels, a clean washing basin, and a dry platform with two low seats give the bath privacy and practical order. Moss, ochre grass, white wildflowers, and green branches soften the cliffs. Frame a narrow opening toward the surrounding mist without copying a famous inn or terrace; the focus is intimate water, warmth, and screened rest.
proposals.context: Warm vapor gathers above the pool and beads on the reed screens. The washing basin sits on the dry side, beside folded towels and a low seat; the sheltered platform leaves room to rest without entering the water. Mineral stains trace the stone lip, and the cool mountain air makes every rising plume visible. A narrow opening gives a glimpse of grey cliffs through the mist, while the screens draw this small enclosure inward toward bodily comfort and private conversation.
proposals.availability: Only d_veiled_stair; an accessible hot spring with a maintained bathing enclosure. Household, guest, or communal access and privacy customs govern admission.

proposals.label: Cliffside Load-Hoist House
proposals.imageDirection: A compact timber service house above a Veiled Stair cliff, housing a heavy rope drum, wooden gearing, broad load baskets, and an open shaft toward a lower terrace. Curved Pandarian roof brackets and a thick straw roof soften an otherwise muscular utility structure. Grey rock, dripping moss, pale-barked trees, and mist appear through the shuttered loading opening. Include spare rope coils, leather hand pads, counterweights, and marked storage cubbies, with a dry inspection bench beside a lattice screen. The scene should communicate an ingenious local response to steep elevation, designed for provisions and equipment rather than spectacular transport machinery.
proposals.context: The rope drum fills much of the service house, its worn fibers carrying the smells of wet hemp and stored grain. Broad baskets wait beside the loading opening, and counterweights hang within the shaft. A screened inspection bench keeps papers and smaller parcels away from the moving gear. Mist curls in whenever the shutter is opened toward the lower terrace. Here a change in elevation becomes a practical household problem of weight, packing, rope wear, and access to the next sheltered landing.
proposals.availability: Only d_veiled_stair; an inhabited cliffside holding with an established goods hoist linking actual terraces. Extrapolated local infrastructure, not a mandatory regional building. Working mechanism and access depend on its owner.

proposals.label: Mist-House Correspondence Room
proposals.imageDirection: A secluded side room in a Veiled Stair residence, its stout timber and pale plaster enclosed beneath steep mountain eaves. A low writing desk holds inkstones, rolled route sketches, message tubes, folded letters, and a small locked document box. Thick curtains and an interior reed screen divide it from the corridor; two cushions face each other beside a covered tea tray. Outside a narrow lattice window, pale-barked branches disappear into grey cliff mist. Warm lantern light, ochre textiles, and dark red joinery create a close, practical interior for confidential household business rather than a spacious guest hall.
proposals.context: The window admits soft grey light and the faint sound of water beyond the eaves. Inkstones, folded letters, and message tubes occupy the desk, with a small locked box beneath its edge. The covered tea tray and facing cushions leave enough space for a close conversation. Curtains deaden the corridor's noise, and the reed screen turns the doorway away from the writing surface. The room's compactness makes every open document and every change in access immediately apparent.
proposals.availability: Only d_veiled_stair; a literate household or institution with a private correspondence room. Inner household admission and authority to view documents are required.

proposals.label: Tidepool Gathering Shelf
proposals.imageDirection: A shallow coastal gathering shelf on the Broken Shore, where low tide exposes dark rocks, clear pools, kelp ribbons, and clustered shellfish below salt-weathered pale elven fragments. Stout baskets, long gathering hooks, a small rinsing trough, and flat sorting stones show an ordinary local food resource. proposals.label: Old Mosaic Repair Room
proposals.imageDirection: A modest craft room on the Broken Shore devoted to repairing inherited elven mosaics and decorative stone panels. Pale arched masonry surrounds sorted trays of colored tesserae, fragments of curved floor borders, fine chisels, lime pots, and careful rubbing sheets. A partly completed panel rests flat on a padded workbench; restrained turquoise and gold fragments recall the lost architecture's sophistication. Through a narrow window lie dark coastal rocks and grey-blue water. Timber roof repairs and a sheltered sample shelf make the ancient room practical again, with sufficient daylight for close handwork and a quiet commission discussion.

Lime pots and chisels occupy the working side; the sheltered sample shelf presents finished fragments without opening the whole floor to visitors. Beyond the narrow window the sea breaks against dark rock. In this close room, repair is measured piece by piece, with the old architecture's surviving patterns held directly in the hand.

proposals.label: Highland Hide Workshop
proposals.imageDirection: A Highmountain leatherworker's sheltered room beneath thick timber and hide roofing, with broad antler-shaped braces, carved posts, and a high open vent toward immense grey peaks. Pine-scented air moves through the high vent, while the clean corner shelters a close discussion of fit, technique, and the marks stitched into the work.

proposals.label: Lower mountain pine woods
proposals.imageDirection: Show thick green pines climbing steep lower Alterac slopes, their trunks broken by gray rock faces and small pockets of tough grass. The ground is angular, root-bound and damp, with pale lichen on shaded stones. Cold blue mist lies below the higher crags; bare rock and possible distant snow show the mountains' vertical scale. Keep the local floor largely snow-free. Build several natural terraces into the foreground, with a close wall of trees uphill and glimpses of a deep valley between trunks downhill.
proposals.context: The pines cling to a slope interrupted by gray rock and shelves of rough grass. Roots hold the damp ground in place, but loose stones shift where the tree cover thins. Cold air drifts upward from the valley, carrying the scent of resin. Uphill, trunks shut out the view; downhill, narrow openings reveal a long drop through blue mist. The slope offers small sheltered terraces, and conversation rises clearly between the rocks whenever the branches stop moving.

proposals.label: Exposed gray high country
proposals.imageDirection: Create a stern Alterac mountain landscape of broken gray ridges, scree fans and narrow grassy shelves, with isolated pines surviving in protected creases. Distant ridges overlap in cold blue haze beneath a heavy sky. Use weathered stone, pale lichen and tough dark vegetation, avoiding permanent snow on every surface. Wind exposure should be visible in low, flattened growth. The foreground contains a broad rock shoulder and a recessed pocket beside an outcrop; open mountain views dominate without centering a pass, tower or travel route.
proposals.context: Gray ridges rise around shelves of thin grass and loose, sharp stone. Wind crosses the exposed shoulders with a low whistle, then drops away abruptly behind an outcrop. The open ground makes movement visible at a distance, although each ridge conceals whatever lies beyond its crest. Footing changes from solid stone to sliding scree within a few steps. Protected cracks hold small pines and the faint smell of resin; elsewhere, the air is cold and bare.

proposals.label: Upper snowfields and ice-crusted crags
proposals.imageDirection: Make upper Alterac unmistakably cold: thick white snow gathered against dark gray crags, blue-shadowed hollows, glazed rock and a few stunted pines bent under ice. Keep the composition broad enough for repeated high mountain locations, with several ridges fading into pale cloud and windblown snow. Use contrasting hard rock shoulders and softer drifts, leaving a sheltered recess on one side. Fine powder streams across exposed ground. The only traces of use are occasional compressed patches in the snow, not a prescribed trail or institution.
proposals.context: Snow fills the hollows between dark crags, blue in the shade and dazzling where the cloud thins. Wind lifts fine powder from the exposed shoulders and drives it against the ice-laden pines. Hard crust supports a step until a deeper drift gives way beneath it. The ridges offer wide views in clear air, then vanish behind blowing snow. A rock recess cuts the wind sharply, making breath and quiet speech audible against the distant hiss of the heights.
